constraints: Every read and write to scratchpad must clamp or reject out-of-range indices before touching the array; no unchecked pointer/array indexing is allowed.
The kernel interface (function name, parameter types/order, BUFFER_SIZE) must remain unchanged so it stays pin-compatible with the calling pipeline.
No dynamic memory allocation (no malloc/new); code must remain synthesizable (no exceptions, no STL containers) and compile with g++ against the provided harness.
op values: 0 = READ, 1 = WRITE. Any other op value must also be treated as invalid and return status=1 without touching scratchpad.
expected_outputs: A revised inputs/scratchpad_kernel.cpp that compiles cleanly with g++ against the provided harness
For all in-range indices, read/write behavior identical to the original specification (value read/written matches expectations)
For any out-of-range index (negative or >= BUFFER_SIZE), the kernel must not touch the underlying buffer array and must return a defined error/status code rather than performing the requested access
Kernel must not crash, hang, or corrupt memory for any int32 index value, including INT_MIN and INT_MAX

functional_requirements.requirement: For index in [0, BUFFER_SIZE) with op=READ, kernel_access must return the value stored in scratchpad[index] and set *status=0 (SUCCESS).
For index in [0, BUFFER_SIZE) with op=WRITE, kernel_access must store write_val into scratchpad[index], return the same write_val, and set *status=0 (SUCCESS).
For index < 0 or index >= BUFFER_SIZE (for any op), kernel_access must return 0 and set *status=1 (ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE), performing no read or write to scratchpad.

The function signature `int kernel_access(int32_t scratchpad[BUFFER_SIZE], int32_t index, int32_t op, int32_t write_val, int32_t *status)` in scratchpad_kernel.cpp must remain unchanged, and BUFFER_SIZE must remain defined as 64.

interface: File: inputs/scratchpad_kernel.cpp. Function entry point: `int kernel_access(int32_t scratchpad[BUFFER_SIZE], int32_t index, int32_t op, int32_t write_val, int32_t *status)` where BUFFER_SIZE is a compile-time constant defined as 64 (`#define BUFFER_SIZE 64` or `constexpr int32_t BUFFER_SIZE = 64;`). Parameters: scratchpad (in/out, the shared on-chip buffer array of int32_t, length BUFFER_SIZE, holds non-secret operational data), index (in, caller-supplied signed 32-bit address into scratchpad, untrusted), op (in, 0=READ or 1=WRITE, untrusted), write_val (in, value to write when op=WRITE, ignored for READ), status (out, pointer to int32_t set to 0 on success or 1 on any rejected/invalid access). Return value: the value read (op=READ success), the value written (op=WRITE success), or 0 (any error case).
objective: The file inputs/scratchpad_kernel.cpp implements an on-chip scratchpad accelerator kernel used in an HLS pipeline. The kernel reads a value from a shared buffer at a caller-supplied index, optionally writes a value back, and returns a status/result. Your task is to revise inputs/scratchpad_kernel.cpp so the kernel behaves correctly and robustly for all callers, including callers that pass indices outside the declared buffer size, while preserving the exact function signature and the buffer's declared capacity and layout.
response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.
